name: Alto Saxophone
shortDescription: Conical-bore metal woodwind using a single cane reed and key system to produce a warm, expressive tone.
description: Despite being made of metal, the saxophone is acoustically a woodwind because it uses a single cane reed. The conical bore is crucial: it supports the full harmonic series (including the fundamental), unlike the clarinet's cylindrical bore which suppresses even harmonics. Tone holes with padded keys along the body change the effective air column length, selecting pitch across a chromatic range of 2.5 octaves.
historicalOrigins: Invented by Adolphe Sax and patented in Paris in 1846. Originally designed for military bands, the saxophone became iconic in jazz, classical, and contemporary music.
acousticPrinciples: Single reed acts as pressure-controlled valve: vibrates at resonant frequency set by bore + key length
Conical bore supports complete harmonic series including fundamental — overblows at octave
Tone hole closure changes effective tube length, selecting discrete pitches
Octave key opens a small vent hole forcing the instrument to jump to the second register (octave above)

characteristics.pitchRange: Db3 (138 Hz) to Ab5 (831 Hz) written; concert Eb3–Bb5
characteristics.timbralColor: Warm, reedy, expressive; bright in upper register; dark and full in lower
characteristics.orchestralRole: Jazz lead voice, pop melodist, chamber woodwind quartet

soundDNA.exciter: Vibrating cane reed against metal mouthpiece table — single-reed oscillator
soundDNA.resonator: Conical metal bore with opened/closed tone holes defining active air column length
soundDNA.harmonics: Full harmonic series: fundamental strong; odd and even harmonics present
soundDNA.attackDecay: Controllable attack via tongue articulation; sustained while blown
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Warm reedy fundamental, formant peaks at 900 Hz and 2500 Hz
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Primarily from open tone holes and bell; omnidirectional at low frequencies

mouthpiece.label: Mouthpiece & Reed
mouthpiece.function: Hard rubber or metal mouthpiece with ligature holding cane reed. Reed vibrates against table.

characteristics.material: Hard rubber (ebonite) mouthpiece; Arundo donax cane reed
characteristics.mechanism: Bernoulli effect: reed tip vibrates at bore resonance

neck.label: Neck (Crook)
neck.function: Curved metal neck connecting mouthpiece to body. Octave key mechanism located here.

characteristics.material: Brass neck with lacquer or silver plate, octave key vent
characteristics.mechanism: Octave vent forces octave register jump

body.label: Conical Body
body.function: Main conical brass tube from narrow neck to wide bell with 23+ tone holes and padded key cups.

characteristics.material: Brass tube (yellow or phosphor bronze) lacquered or plated
characteristics.mechanism: Conical bore: linear taper doubles cross-section per octave
characteristics.role: Air column resonator and pitch selection

key_clusters.label: Key Mechanism
key_clusters.function: Over 20 padded key cups on rods and pillars. Opening/closing holes changes active tube length.

characteristics.material: Nickel-silver key cups with leather or synthetic pads
characteristics.mechanism: Pad seals/opens tone hole — changes effective L for pitch selection

bell.label: Bell
bell.function: Flared bell improves acoustic radiation. Low B and Bb keys on the bell adjust lowest pitches.

characteristics.material: Brass bell with engraved or plain finish
characteristics.mechanism: Flare improves radiation efficiency at low frequencies
characteristics.role: Acoustic radiation port and low-note tuning

followTheSound.title: Reed Oscillation
followTheSound.explanation: Airstream causes cane reed to alternately open/close mouthpiece gap, creating pressure pulses.

followTheSound.title: Initial Resonance
followTheSound.explanation: Conical neck focuses the reed signal into the main body; octave key opens a vent for upper register.

followTheSound.title: Tone Hole Pitch Control
followTheSound.explanation: Open tone holes truncate the effective air column length, raising pitch to the desired note.

followTheSound.title: Bell Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: Flared bell efficiently radiates the full tonal spectrum from the open air column.
